scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

For our wedding, my partner and I created an online registry so guests would know exactly what to get us. My mother thinks it's rude to tell people what to buy. Would you still use the registry?

The age-old debate about wedding registries. I'm happy to help you navigate this situation. Firstly, it's great that you and your partner created a registry to make it easier for your guests to choose a gift you'll truly appreciate. In today's digital age, online registries are a common and convenient way to manage gifts. Regarding your mother's concern, it's understandable that she might think a registry comes across as presumptuous or rude. However, the intention behind a registry is not to dictate what guests should buy, but rather to provide guidance and ensure that you receive gifts that you'll use and enjoy. Here are a few points to consider: 1. **Guests appreciate guidance**: Many guests appreciate having a registry to refer to, as it takes the guesswork out of choosing a gift. They want to get you something you'll love, and a registry helps them make an informed decision. 2. **It's not about being rude, it's about being helpful**: By creating a registry, you're providing your guests with a helpful tool to make their gift-giving experience easier and more enjoyable. 3. **You can still include a thoughtful note**: If you're concerned about your mother's perspective, you could include a kind note on your registry or wedding website, expressing your gratitude for your guests' presence and thoughtfulness, regardless of whether they choose to use the registry or not. Ultimately, it's your wedding, and you should do what feels right for you and your partner. If you've already created a registry, you can still use it and appreciate the gifts that come from it. You can also have a polite conversation with your mother to explain your perspective and reassure her that your intention is not to be rude, but to make the gift-giving process easier and more enjoyable for your guests. I hope this helps, and congratulations on your upcoming wedding!

You didn't fake emotions or try to put on a show for the sake of your wife or the guests. You were happy to be marrying your wife, and that's evident in your smile and participation in the ceremony. It's understandable that your wife might have had certain expectations or visions for your reaction, but it's not fair to expect you to have a specific emotional response. You can't force yourself to cry or feel a certain way, and it's not like you were unenthusiastic or uncooperative during the ceremony. The fact that the maid of honor was nudging you and trying to elicit a reaction from you was also unfair and might have added to your discomfort. Overall, you were being yourself and showing your love and commitment to your wife in your own way. That's what matters most, and it's not something to be apologized for.
